issues.description: The type of StockIngredient.price is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement UML declares price as int, the template StockIngredient.java defines price as double, while the solution StockIngredient.java uses int. This mismatch can confuse students when they implement SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice (which expect integer prices per the specification) and when constructing StockIngredient instances.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the StockIngredient.price type consistent. Preferably update the template StockIngredient.java to use int for price (including constructor parameter and getPrice return type) to match the UML in problem_statement.md and the solution. Alternatively, if double prices are intended, update the problem statement and the solution to use double consistently and adjust calculateTotalPrice/acceptSupplyDelivery signatures/docs accordingly.

issues.description: The StockIngredient 'price' attribute/constructor parameter is represented with inconsistent types across artifacts: the problem statement UML and the solution expect an int price (StockIngredient(String, int, int)), whereas the template StockIngredient uses a double price (constructor StockIngredient(String, double, int) and getPrice() returns double). This mismatch between the template and the problem/solution creates confusion for students about the intended type of the 'price' field and the return type of getPrice(), increasing cognitive load when mapping requirements to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the 'price' type consistent across all artifacts. Either update the template StockIngredient to use an int price (change the field, constructor parameter, and getPrice() return type to int) to match the problem statement and solution, or if double is intended, update the problem statement and solution to use double. Prefer aligning the template to the problem statement/solution (int) to avoid student confusion.
